A negative sentiment analysis (NSA) refers to an approach that analyzes how people feel about something or someone by looking at their words rather than actions . It can be used for various purposes such as marketing research , customer service improvement programs etc., but its main goal remains unchanged: To provide valuable insights into what customers think of your brand so you know where improvements need made before they become unhappy clients who leave bad reviews online!

What Is Sentiment Analysis?
Sentiment analysis is a technique used to analyze opinions expressed through language using natural language processing techniques .
It involves analyzing large amounts of unstructured data from social media platforms like Twitter, Facebook posts, blogs comments sections among other places where users express themselves freely over time periods ranging anywhere between minutes up until years depending upon factors including topic relevance & volume being analyzed amongst many others too numerous mention right now 😉
This type method helps identify trends within specific topics across multiple sources simultaneously allowing organizations gain deeper insight regarding public perception toward particular products/services offered thus enabling better decision making processes going forward based off accurate feedback provided via automated tools designed specifically catered needs unique individuals/groups involved therein process itself !

There are two types of NSAs : supervised learning algorithms and unsupervised machine-learning models . Supervised Learning Algorithms require labeled training sets while Unsupervised Models do not have labels attached beforehand during development phase instead relying solely upon existing patterns found throughout dataset(s). -Requires human intervention prior implementation stage i.e labeling all relevant sentences manually first thing after collecting initial set raw texts then feeding these preprocessed documents
